title: HMOX1 controls a heme-ferritin switch that protects cells from ferroptosis.
takeaway: Reports that when HMOX1 is inactive, heme is stabilized rather than catabolised, and that this stabilized heme up-regulates ferritin and suppresses ferroptosis, rescuing cell death caused by both pharmacological and genetic GPX4 inhibition. The authors frame this as a heme-HMOX1-ferritin axis setting ferroptosis sensitivity.
caveat: The abstract describes cell-level experiments only and names no tumour model or in vivo test; the therapeutic use it raises is proposed, not shown.

title: Metabolic rewiring driven by phosphoglycolate phosphatase deletion inhibits ferroptosis.
takeaway: Deleting phosphoglycolate phosphatase (PGP) suppresses ferroptosis by rewiring the pentose phosphate pathway and cellular energy and lipid metabolism into a multifactorial antioxidant response. Separately, the reported PGP inhibitor CP1 turns out to sensitize cells to ferroptosis and is characterized as a direct dual inhibitor of PGP and FSP1 that also triggers FSP1 self-assembly.
caveat: The abstract names genetic, biochemical and biophysical approaches without saying which experimental system each was done in, and mentions no animal or disease model, so CP1 is presented as a pharmacological tool rather than a validated therapeutic.

title: Ferroptosis induction via genetic approaches - CRISPR/Cas9-based disruption on key anti-ferroptotic genes.
takeaway: A methods chapter, not new findings: it sets out a CRISPR/Cas9 protocol for making SLC7A11- and GPX4-knockout HT1080 cells as a genetic alternative to erastin and (1S,3R)-RSL3, whose off-target effects the authors note (erastin on mitochondrial voltage-dependent anion channels, RSL3 on other selenoproteins). The knockout lines need beta-mercaptoethanol or liproxstatin-1 in the medium, and withdrawing the supplement induces ferroptosis.
caveat: This is a protocol chapter rather than a report of new results: the abstract describes a procedure in one cell line (HT1080), so it is a method to use, not evidence about ferroptosis biology.

title: Double-bond geometry determines fatty acid metabolic fate and ferroptosis sensitivity.
takeaway: A screen of structurally diverse fatty acids identifies trans-unsaturated fatty acids as ferroptosis sensitizers: the trans PUFA linoelaidic acid enhanced lipid peroxidation more than its cis counterpart linoleic acid, and the trans monounsaturated petroselaidic acid also sensitized cells while its cis isomer petroselinic acid suppressed ferroptosis. Petroselaidic acid required stearoyl-CoA desaturase-dependent conversion to a PUFA, which the authors read as double-bond geometry redirecting a fatty acid metabolic fate.
caveat: A preprint, so not yet peer reviewed, and the abstract reports cell-level lipidomic and sensitivity experiments with no animal or dietary model, leaving any physiological consequence of trans-fat geometry untested.

title: 15-LOX-catalytic bias towards ether-(alkenyl)-ETE-PEs oxidation bestows selectivity of PRO-ferroptotic cell death signaling.
takeaway: Using redox lipidomics with biochemical, biophysical, genetic and molecular dynamics approaches, the authors find both 15-LOX isoforms selectively oxidize alkyl/alkenyl-ETE-PE, but not the PC equivalents, to 15-HpETE-PEs and trigger ferroptosis independently of the sn-1 vinyl bond. They measure sn-1 vinyl bond peroxidation as roughly 500-fold slower than sn-2-ETE-PE, which they take to exclude an antioxidant role for plasmalogens in ferroptosis, and report the sn-1-alkenyl-sn-2-15-HpETE-PE product as a pathogenic factor in asthma, cancer, brain trauma and skin UVB injury.
caveat: The abstract asserts the oxidized lipid acts as a pathogenic factor in those four settings without describing the experiments behind it, so what was measured, tested or blocked in each is left unspecified, and the therapeutic target it proposes is untested.

title: Targeted extracellular degradation of LRP8 promotes ferroptosis in cancer cells.
takeaway: Targeted extracellular degradation of the selenium uptake receptor LRP8, using bispecific KineTAC chimeras that route it to the lysosome through cytokine receptor internalisation, lowers several selenoproteins including GPX4 and sensitizes cancer cells to ferroptosis. The authors present receptor-mediated selenium uptake as a targetable node in ferroptosis resistance.
caveat: A preprint, so not yet peer reviewed, and the abstract reports sensitization in cancer cells with no in vivo efficacy, selectivity or toxicity data, so overcoming therapy resistance is framed as a broader prospect rather than a result.

title: Polyamines buffer labile iron to suppress ferroptosis.
takeaway: Polyamines are shown to buffer redox-active iron: a genome-wide CRISPR screen found polyamine depletion synthetically lethal with loss of GPX4, and polyamine deficiency redistributed cellular iron, enlarging the labile iron pool and up-regulating ferritin. A new genetically encoded fluorescent reporter for redox-active iron showed an inverse correlation between polyamine levels and redox-active iron in single living cells.
caveat: The abstract reports cultured-cell screening and live-cell imaging only; the implications it draws for ferroptosis-linked disease states are stated as implications, with no animal or patient data behind them.

title: Suppression of Lipid Peroxidation by Necrostatins and Their Potential for Dual Targeting of Ferroptosis and Necroptosis.
takeaway: Explains how the RIPK1 inhibitor necrostatin-1 also blocks ferroptosis: its thiohydantoin reacts with hydroperoxides to give a sulfenic acid that traps peroxyl radicals and inhibits lipid peroxidation. Analogs tested in the cell-free FENIX assay gained anti-peroxidation activity with more steric bulk or nucleophilicity near the thiocarbonyl, with the methyl group relocated, or with a fully conjugated linker; the fully conjugated dsNec-1, isolated as a stable species, is suggested to mediate the anti-ferroptotic effect, but desaturated derivatives were inactive against necroptosis, so the authors conclude the scaffold is unsuitable for dual-pathway inhibitors.
caveat: The structure-activity work rests on the cell-free FENIX lipid peroxidation assay, and the abstract reports no cellular ferroptosis protection for the new analogs, so dsNec-1 mediating Nec-1 activity in cells is suggested rather than shown.

title: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression.
takeaway: Reports KY0418, an orally dosed, plasma-stable covalent GPX4 inhibitor with an isourea warhead that targets GPX4 at SeCys46 and induces ferroptosis hallmarks in human and mouse cancer cell lines with greater selectivity than existing inhibitors. In mice it reproduces ferroptotic changes in an acute-liver-injury model, remodels tissue metabolism and generates detectable hydroxyl radicals, and across cancer models consistently eradicated circulating tumor cells and suppressed metastasis.
caveat: Shown in cancer cell lines and in mice; the abstract reports subcutaneous-tumor responses ranged from no effect to about 70% growth inhibition, and positions KY0418 as a tool for in vivo research and translation rather than a treatment tested in patients.

title: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression.
takeaway: Describes designed mitochondria-targeting tetraoxane compounds (WMK-1/2) that initiate local lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis without first inhibiting GPX4 or FSP1. The abstract reports WMK-1 localizes to mitochondria, impairs oxidative phosphorylation, and drives a labile-Fe2+-dependent "mito-ferroptosis" that is rescued by lipophilic radical-trapping antioxidants and by alpha-lipoic acid but is insensitive to ACSL4 perturbation and PUFA supplementation; WMK-1/2 are bioavailable, suppress tumors, and augment immune-checkpoint blockers.
caveat: The GPX4/FSP1-independent sub-pathway rests on the rescue and perturbation experiments the abstract lists, and efficacy is reported in cell and mouse cancer models, not in patients.

title: Pooled Screening of Cancer Cell Lines Identifies Vulnerability to Polyunsaturated Fatty-Acid-Induced Ferroptosis.
takeaway: A barcoded, pooled screen across 554 cancer cell lines from 19 lineages finds a subset sensitive to polyunsaturated fatty acids at physiological concentrations, with PUFA treatment alone sufficient to induce ferroptosis in lines that are also vulnerable to GPX4 inhibition. PUFA sensitivity is positively associated with FABP1 expression, conjugated linolenic acids also induce ferroptosis, and a genome-wide CRISPR screen in ES2 cells defines a pro-ferroptosis route converting PUFAs to membrane phospholipids and an anti-ferroptosis route diverting them to lipid droplets.
caveat: The dataset is cultured cell lines; the FABP1 link is reported as a positive association across lines rather than a tested mechanism, and the abstract suggests the dietary-metabolite therapeutic avenue rather than showing it in animals.

title: Mammals produce cyclo-octasulfur to suppress lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis.
takeaway: Reports that mammals harbor elemental sulfur as cyclo-octasulfur (S8), accumulating to millimolar concentrations in mitochondrial membranes and lipid droplets of mouse and human cells, and identifies lipid-droplet-associated nitric oxide synthase as a source of its biosynthesis. S8 in lipid droplets limits lipid peroxidation and suppresses ferroptosis, and intra-articular injection of solubilized S8 reduced lipid peroxidation in a mouse osteoarthritis model.
caveat: Based on mouse and human cells plus one osteoarthritis mouse model where injected S8 lowered lipid peroxidation, a redox readout rather than a disease outcome; the abstract states the protective role as one S8 "may" play.

title: Targeted extracellular degradation of LRP8 promotes ferroptosis in cancer cells.
takeaway: Identifies targeted extracellular degradation of the selenium-uptake receptor LRP8 as a way to lower the ferroptosis-protective enzyme GPX4: bispecific KineTAC chimeras couple LRP8 to cytokine-receptor internalization and route it to the lysosome, reducing several selenoproteins including GPX4 and sensitizing cancer cells to ferroptosis. The authors frame receptor-mediated selenium uptake as a targetable node in ferroptosis resistance.
caveat: The results the abstract describes are at the cell level (reduced selenoprotein abundance and sensitization of cancer cells); overcoming therapy resistance is presented as a framework the approach could enable, not a demonstrated outcome.

title: On the Inhibition of Lipid Peroxidation and Ferroptosis by Fatty Acids.
takeaway: Tests whether replacing oxidizable PUFAs with non-oxidizable fatty acids is a general way to suppress ferroptosis by preparing cyclopropanated PUFAs (CP-PUFAs), predicted to be far less reactive to peroxyl radicals while keeping cis geometry. CP-PUFAs suppressed erastin2- and RSL3-induced ferroptosis in HT-1080 and HEK-293 cells much as deuterated PUFAs and MUFAs did while palmitate did not, with CP2-LA comparable to D-PUFAs but CP4-AA only modest, and lipidomics showed accompanying lipid remodeling.
caveat: Tested in two cultured cell lines against two chemical inducers; the authors state the strategy is general only provided the non-oxidizable fatty acid can be used by biosynthetic machinery and is not lipotoxic at the concentrations needed for protection.

title: PLA2G2F suppresses ferroptosis through phospholipid remodeling.
takeaway: Identifies the secretory phospholipase PLA2G2F as a ferroptosis suppressor in bladder cancer that acts intracellularly from the endoplasmic reticulum. The abstract reports that PPARG upregulates PLA2G2F and that PPARG-mediated ferroptosis resistance largely depends on it, that lipidomic profiling indicates PLA2G2F preferentially acts on ether-linked PUFA phospholipids to shrink the peroxidation-prone pool, and that inhibiting PPARG signaling or PLA2G2F sensitizes bladder cancer cells to ferroptosis.
caveat: Shown in bladder cancer; the preferential action on ether-linked PUFA phospholipids is what the abstract says the lipidomic profiling "suggests," and the sensitization is reported in bladder cancer cells.

title: Cell-state-specific metabolic networks govern ferroptosis versus apoptosis in small cell lung cancer.
takeaway: In small cell lung cancer, integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis finds a universal dependency on exogenous cysteine/cystine across neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine states. On cysteine depletion, ASCL1-low cells undergo ferroptosis while ASCL1-high cells undergo apoptosis and resist ferroptosis, a resistance the abstract attributes to ASCL1 directly activating GCH1 and raising BH4/BH2 antioxidants; combining cysteine depletion with inhibition of BH4/BH2 synthesis reduced tumor growth in patient-derived xenografts.
caveat: Demonstrated in small cell lung cancer models, including defined cell states and patient-derived xenografts; the cell-death switch and the ASCL1-GCH1-BH4 mechanism are shown for SCLC and not claimed beyond it.
